clinician.trajectory_summary: A 65-year-old male presented with a 3-week history of red-eye and was found on examination to have a firm, oval, dark brown, vascular, dome-shaped, non-mobile, lobulated subconjunctival mass in the right eye measuring 7×6×3.2 mm. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 bilaterally with no epiphora, pain, or photophobia. Dilated fundoscopy and gonioscopy were normal with no evidence of intraocular extension. Systemic examination was normal. Initial clinical diagnosis was presumed conjunctival malignant melanoma based on the dark appearance and vascularity. The patient underwent excisional biopsy with no-touch technique, 3 mm margin, partial sclerectomy, and cryotherapy. Intraoperative examination confirmed no intraocular extension. Histopathology with hematoxylin and eosin staining revealed large vascular channels lined by endothelial cells and filled with red blood cells separated by fibrous interstitium, with no sign of malignancy or necrosis. This histopathologic finding confirmed the diagnosis of cavernous hemangioma. At 6-month follow-up, the patient showed no sign of recurrence.
